title: Blur Generator
subtitle: Bad photos on purpose, for training models
description: Makes perfectly good images worse on purpose: motion, lens, Gaussian and depth-aware blur, for training models that have to cope with bad photos.
longDescription: A comprehensive image processing tool that generates various types of blur effects including motion blur, lens blur, and gaussian blur using OpenCV. This tool is particularly useful for data augmentation in machine learning projects and creating realistic image effects.
results: Widely used in ML data augmentation
why: The blur detector from the Infortrend vision work needed blurry photos to learn from, and real cameras only take those when nobody wants them. Blur Generator makes them on demand from sharp images: motion, lens or Gaussian, with the strength as a number, or varied by depth with a depth map.
gains: For anyone training blur detection or deblurring models: every sharp photo becomes as many blurred copies as needed, each with a known type and strength. With a depth map and a focus point it also fakes a portrait mode, no new phone required.

lessons: Up to 1.2.0 a decimal lens radius blurred like the next whole number: 2.5 gave the picture of 3. It now lands in between.
With the default sigma of 5, Gaussian kernels wider than about 31 px all look the same; sigma=0 lets the kernel size set the strength.
min_blur=0 used to crash motion and lens blur by depth; a blur amount of 0 now simply means an untouched copy.
